### Load libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(themis)
library(ranger)
library(knitr)
library(pROC)
library(glmnet)
set.seed(381)
```

### 1.1Load data and objects from Milestone 2

```{r}
split    <- readRDS("../my_datasets/split.rds")
rec_prep <- readRDS("../my_datasets/recipe_prep.rds")

train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)
```

### 1.2 Class distribution

```{r}
cat("===== Train set =====\n")
print(table(train_data$vulnerable))
print(prop.table(table(train_data$vulnerable)))

cat("\n===== Test set =====\n")
print(table(test_data$vulnerable))
print(prop.table(table(test_data$vulnerable)))


```

### Remove leakage variables

The target variable vulnerable was constructed in Milestone 2 using three derived indicators: low services access, food insecurity, and low income.

The original variables that were used to create those indicators (for example water source, toilet type, electricity access, income, and hunger codes) were removed from the modelling dataset.

This step prevents data leakage, ensuring that the models are evaluated on genuine predictive patterns rather than simply reconstructing the target from the same information that defined it.

```{r}
leakage_vars <- c(
  # Services used for services_access_score
  "drinking_water_source_code", "piped_water_code", "main_toilet_code",
  "shared_toilet_code", "electricity_access_code", "toilet_location_code",
  "handwashing_facility_code", "water_safe_code", "water_interruptions12months_code",
  
  # Income used for low_income
  "total_monthly_household_income_raw", "income_per_capita",
  "main_income_source_code", "required_income_raw", "comparative_income_code",
  
  # Hunger / food variables
  "adult_hunger_code", "child_hunger_code",
  "worried_food_would_run_out_code", "unable_to_eat_healthy_food_code",
  "ate_few_foods_code", "skipped_meal_code", "ate_less_code",
  "ran_out_of_food_code", "hungry_but_did_not_eat_code", "whole_day_without_eating_code",
  
  # Derived columns
  "services_access_score", "food_insecure_flag", "low_income", "overcrowding"
)

# Also drop any remaining columns that still contain these keywords
extra_drop <- names(train_data)[
  str_detect(names(train_data),
             regex("water|toilet|electric|income|hunger|food|grant|salary|asset|fridge|washing|geyser|freezer|services_access|food_insecure|low_income|overcrowd",
                   ignore_case = TRUE))
]

cols_to_drop <- unique(c(leakage_vars, extra_drop))

train_data <- train_data %>% select(-any_of(cols_to_drop))
test_data  <- test_data  %>% select(-any_of(cols_to_drop))

cat("Remaining columns after leakage removal:\n")
print(names(train_data))

```

```{r}
rec <- recipe(vulnerable ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_smote(vulnerable, over_ratio = 1)

```

### 1.3 Logistic Regression

```{r}
log_fit <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(
    logistic_reg(penalty = 0.01, mixture = 1) %>%   # Lasso
      set_engine("glmnet")
  ) %>%
  add_recipe(rec) %>%
  fit(data = train_data)
```

### 1.4 Random Forest

```{r}
rf_fit <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(
    rand_forest(trees = 800, mtry = 8, min_n = 8) %>%
      set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
      set_mode("classification")
  ) %>%
  add_recipe(rec) %>%
  fit(data = train_data)

```

### 2. Prepare predictions on the TEST set

```{r}
log_pred <- predict(log_fit, test_data, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(predict(log_fit, test_data)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_data %>% select(vulnerable))

rf_pred <- predict(rf_fit, test_data, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(predict(rf_fit, test_data)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_data %>% select(vulnerable))
```

### 3. Confusion Matrices

```{r}
cat("\n===== Logistic Regression =====\n")
cm_log <- conf_mat(log_pred, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class)
print(cm_log)

cat("\n===== Random Forest =====\n")
cm_rf <- conf_mat(rf_pred, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class)
print(cm_rf)
```

### 4. Performance metrics

```{r}
# Create metrics
get_metrics <- function(pred_df) {
  tibble(
    Accuracy          = accuracy(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class)$.estimate,
    Balanced_Accuracy = bal_accuracy(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class)$.estimate,
    Precision         = precision(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class, event_level = "second")$.estimate,
    Recall            = recall(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class, event_level = "second")$.estimate,
    Specificity       = spec(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class, event_level = "second")$.estimate,
    F1                = f_meas(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, estimate = .pred_class, event_level = "second")$.estimate,
    ROC_AUC           = roc_auc(pred_df, truth = vulnerable, `.pred_Vulnerable`)$.estimate
  )
}

metrics_log <- get_metrics(log_pred) %>% mutate(Model = "Logistic Regression", .before = 1)
metrics_rf  <- get_metrics(rf_pred)  %>% mutate(Model = "Random Forest", .before = 1)

# Create the comparison matrix
comparison_matrix <- bind_rows(metrics_log, metrics_rf) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

print(comparison_matrix)
kable(comparison_matrix, caption = "Model Comparison / Validation Matrix (Test Set)")
```

### 5. ROC Curves

```{r}
# Create the ROC objects
actual_bin <- ifelse(test_data$vulnerable == "Vulnerable", 1, 0)

roc_log <- roc(actual_bin, log_pred$.pred_Vulnerable, quiet = TRUE)
roc_rf  <- roc(actual_bin, rf_pred$.pred_Vulnerable,  quiet = TRUE)

# Plot
plot(roc_log, col = "darkorange", lwd = 2,
     main = "ROC Curves – Test Set",
     xlim = c(1, 0), ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlab = "1 - Specificity", ylab = "Sensitivity",
     legacy.axes = TRUE)
plot(roc_rf, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey")
legend("bottomright",
       legend = c(
         paste0("Logistic Regression (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_log), 3), ")"),
         paste0("Random Forest (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_rf), 3), ")")
       ),
       col = c("darkorange", "steelblue"), lwd = 2)
```

### 7. Save final objects for Task 4

```{r}
saveRDS(rf_fit, "final_model.rds")
saveRDS(rec, "final_recipe.rds")
write_csv(comparison_matrix, "model_comparison_matrix.csv")
```

After removing variables that were used to construct the target (to prevent data leakage), both models were evaluated on the held-out test set.

Logistic Regression achieved an AUC of 0.605, while Random Forest achieved an AUC of 0.93.

Because the business objective is to identify vulnerable households so that support can be prioritised, higher Recall, F1-score and ROC-AUC are preferred.
